name: Payam
source: Wiktionary, Persian پیام (payâm): Iran formal [pʰæ.jɒ́ːm], Dari [pʰä.jɑ́ːm]; stress on the last syllable
notes: Persian â [ɒː] has no English match: English 'ah' (US ɑ, GB ɑː) is the usual approximation.

name: Mohammed
source: Wiktionary, English Mohammed: /məˈhæməd/ (also /mʊəˈhɑːməd/); today's reading differs only in unstressed vowels

alternatives.context: closer to Arabic Muḥammad; many Arabic-speaking bearers

notes: Control: the app's CMUdict reading (mOhˈæmɪd) is an accepted English reading of this spelling.

name: Jesús

alternatives.context: the English name of Jesus of Nazareth; not how bearers of the Spanish name say it

notes: Spanish j [x] becomes English h, as English speakers say it. The accented spelling is only the Spanish name.

name: Søren
notes: Danish ø [ɶː] is a front rounded vowel English lacks; English sources give the 'sorr' approximation.

name: Will
notes: Ordinary word 'will'. The name sounds like the word, but in a sentence the app de-stresses it like the auxiliary verb (I met Will yesterday: wˌɪl).
